hook_text: A bicycle shop does fourteen deals in one month. The scale still balances to the last rand. Watch.
clip_script: Kasi Cycles, Soweto. 1 November: 70 000 of assets equals 62 000 owner's equity plus 8 000 owed to suppliers. Cash sale, R9 000: bank up, stock down 6 000, owner up 3 000. Credit sale to a courier company: debtors up instead of the bank, profit earned anyway. Stock bought on credit: stock up, owed up. A school pays its account: bank up, debtors down, no new income. We pay a supplier: bank down, owed down, no expense. Wages, rent, bank charges: owner's share down. Fourteen transactions later: 73 800 equals 62 800 plus 11 000. The owner grew by R800. And that is exactly the profit. The scale never tips.
visual_style: An old-fashioned balance scale with assets on one pan and owner's equity and liabilities on the other, tokens moving with each transaction, a running total ticking at the bottom.
pacing: One beat per transaction, speeding up through the middle, a slow, satisfying final balance.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and analyse the whole month yourself.
